newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jerusalem mayor must stand trial - attorney-general.
newsitem.headline: Jerusalem mayor must stand trial - attorney-general.

text.p: Jerusalem mayor Ehud Olmert, a leading member of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party, should stand trial for corruption, Israel's attorney-general said in a decision published on Monday.
"I have concluded that there is enough evidence...to warrant that Knesset-Member Olmert stand trial," Attorney-General Michael Ben-Yair said.

Olmert, a member of Knesset (parliament) for 20 years, is suspected of soliciting illegal donations for Likud while party treasurer during the 1988 election campaign. He is also suspected of giving the state comptroller false financial reports. No charges have been filed against him.
Olmert's office said it had no comment.

But Olmert said in June when it first appeared Ben-Yair would recommend bringing charges: "I think the attorney-general made a terrible mistake and I am absolutely confident that all this will be cleared up soon and that it will be evident that there was no wrong-doing on my behalf."
Ben-Yair said other Likud officials in charge of finances in 1988 had already been convicted.
"The decision (to try Olmert) is required according the principle of equality under the law," he said.
Political commentators said Netanyahu held off giving Olmert a cabinet post in his new government three months ago because of the affair.

Olmert is a central Likud figure and close political associate of Netanyahu. He was a senior minister in the previous Likud government of Yitzhak Shamir. He won Jerusalem for the right-wing by toppling veteran liberal mayor Teddy Kollek.
Olmert enjoys parliamentary immunity from prosecution which Ben-Yair will ask legislators to lift when the Knesset reconvenes next month.
After considering Ben-Yair's decision the Knesset House Committee will decide whether to refer the affair to the full house for a vote.
